source.body:
### Bug Description

On n8n Enterprise, I published a workflow agent to Chat Hub. The workflow
uses a Chat Trigger and an AI Agent with an MCP Client Tool configured for
MCP OAuth2. The credential type is **End-user credential**.

Users with **Full access** can use the published chat and its MCP tool.
Users with the **Chat user** role can see and open the same chat, but
attempting to use the MCP tool results in an OAuth-related error.

### To Reproduce

### Steps to reproduce

1. In a team project, configure an AI Agent with an MCP Client Tool using
   MCP OAuth2 and an End-user credential.
2. Publish the workflow and make it available in Chat Hub.
3. Open the published chat as a user with Full access and send a message
   that invokes the MCP tool. Verify that it works.
4. Open the same chat as a Chat user who can access it and send the same
   message.

### Actual behavior

The chat is visible to the Chat user, but the request fails when using the
MCP tool.

- Exact error: [paste the error with sensitive details removed]
- OAuth consent screen: [not offered / offered but fails / completes before
  the MCP call fails]

### Expected behavior

If this combination is supported, a Chat user who is allowed to use the
workflow should be able to connect their own OAuth account from Chat Hub
and invoke the MCP tool within their own permissions, without being granted
access to edit workflows or credentials.

If this combination is not supported, Chat Hub should show a clear message
explaining the restriction.

### Debug Info

- n8nVersion: 2.49.6
- platform: docker (self-hosted)
- nodeJsVersion: 26.13.0
- nodeEnv: development
- database: postgres
- executionMode: regular
- concurrency: -1
- license: enterprise (production)

### Operating System

docker

26.13.0

PostgreSQL

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: The issue template still has placeholders for the exact error and OAuth-consent outcome. Could you add the sanitized error text and say whether the Chat user sees the consent screen, completes consent, or fails before it appears? Also, does the MCP OAuth credential exist in that Chat user’s personal project, or only on the workflow? Those details should distinguish an OAuth callback/consent problem from credential access being denied during workflow execution.

comments.author: sinehypernova-0718
comments.text:
Hey @emmaanuel, thanks for filing this.

Could you fill in the template when you get a chance? The exact error text would help a lot, with any tokens or account details removed. Also, when the Chat user sends the message, do they see the OAuth consent screen at all? If they do, do they get through it? If it fails before the consent screen shows up, that's useful to know too.

One more thing: does the MCP OAuth credential live in that Chat user's personal project, or only in the project where the workflow sits? That tells us whether this is about access to the credential or about the OAuth flow itself.

If you happen to know whether this worked on an earlier version, that would help us narrow it down as well.

Thanks, really appreciate it.
